topic: A receipt is not a verdict

choices.text: What ran: the command, the inputs and the hash of the output
A reviewer's opinion of the work

holds.note: Whether a claim holds is a verdict, and a verdict needs a criterion. A receipt only records what happened.

opinion.note: A receipt carries no judgement. It is a record a stranger can rerun.

source.quote: A receipt records what ran: the command, the inputs and the hash of the output.

items.prompt: Rerun the command and the hash matches. What does that show?

right.note: A matching hash shows the bytes are the same. Whether they are right needs a criterion the author did not write.

honest.note: A hash says nothing about a person. It fingerprints bytes.

source.quote: That shows the same bytes came out. It says nothing about whether they are right.

items.prompt: What does a verdict need that a receipt does not have?

choices.text: A criterion the author did not write
A second run by the author

longer.note: Hash length changes how hard a forgery is. It does not judge the output.

second-run.note: An author rerunning their own work shows the same bytes again. The criterion has to come from outside the author.

source.quote: A verdict needs a criterion the author did not write, such as a test suite, a proof checker or a measured threshold.

items.prompt: In the example, the rerun matches and the independent test reports drift. What follows?

choices.text: The receipt holds, and the claim fails
Both hold, because the hashes match
Both fail, because the test drifted

both-hold.note: Matching hashes vouch for the record. The test is what judged the claim.

both-fail.note: The drift is a fact about the claim. The receipt still records truthfully what ran.

source.quote: The receipt holds, and the claim fails.
